title: Electronic Conveyancing and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Electronic Conveyancing and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Electronic Conveyancing and Mental Capacity Bill
sections.summary: The Bill amends existing legislation to digitalise property conveyancing and the Lasting Power of Attorney process under the Mental Capacity Act 2008.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To do this, I introduce the Electronic Conveyancing and Other Matters Bill, which will relate to two of the most consequential decisions many of us will make in our lives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Here, the Government proposes to amend existing legislation to facilitate the digitalisation of the property conveyancing process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Here, we introduce amendments to the Mental Capacity Act 2008 to further digitalise the end-to-end process of making a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

sections.label: Digital Conveyancing Portal development
sections.summary: SLA is developing the Digital Conveyancing Portal as a key plank to transform the manual, paper-based conveyancing process into a fully digitalised one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: One key plank in the journey to transform the current manual and paper-based process to a fully digitalised, end-to-end conveyancing process is the development of the Digital Conveyancing Portal (DCP) by SLA.

sections.label: Pilot for Option-to-Purchase stage
sections.summary: A pilot will be launched in early 2026 covering the Option-to-Purchase stage of resale private residential property transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In early 2026, a pilot will be launched to cover the Option-to-Purchase stage of the resale phase of private residential property transactions.

sections.label: Amending ETA with Part 2B
sections.summary: ETA will be amended by adding Part 2B to enable electronic conveyancing through Prescribed Electronic Transaction Systems, initially the DCP and HDB Flat Portal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: ETA will be amended by adding a new Part 2B to enable conveyancing transactions to be executed electronically through the Prescribed Electronic Transaction Systems (PETS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The PETS will be set out in a new Fifth Schedule to the ETA and will initially be confined to two portals – the DCP and the HDB Flat Portal.

sections.label: Remote witnessing under section 16X
sections.summary: New section 16X allows remote witnessing to satisfy legal witnessing requirements for executing a conveyancing document, but only under specific conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new section 16X will allow for remote witnessing as a means to satisfy any legal witnessing requirement in respect of the execution of a conveyancing document, but only under specific conditions.

sections.label: Conditions for electronic deed execution
sections.summary: The electronic record must state it is intended to be a deed, and individual execution requires a secure electronic signature in the PETS before a witness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, the electronic record must clearly state, on its face, that it is a document intended to be a deed, so that there is no ambiguity as to parties' intentions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Third, where the deed is being executed by an individual, the electronic record must be signed in the PETS using a secure electronic signature and the signing must be in the presence of a witness.

sections.label: ETA First Schedule amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the ETA First Schedule to extend Part 2 to certain immovable property contracts and instruments executed in a PETS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will also amend the First Schedule of the ETA to extend the application of Part 2 of the ETA to contracts for the sale or other disposition of immovable property, dispositions of an equitable interest respecting immovable property, conveyances of immovable property, and instruments by deed to secure payment of moneys under a mortgage, that are executed in a PETS.

sections.label: Singapore Land Authority Act amendments
sections.summary: The Singapore Land Authority Act 2001 will be amended to empower SLA to establish the DCP electronic transaction system for conveyancing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In addition to the ETA, amendments to the Singapore Land Authority Act 2001 will be made to empower SLA to establish an electronic transaction system, the DCP, to enable persons to carry out conveyancing transactions using electronic instruments.

sections.label: HDB flat deed execution
sections.summary: The amended Housing and Development Act allows deeds for HDB flat conveyancing to be executed by signature of at least two duly authorised officers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As an alternative to the common seal, the amended Housing and Development Act will also allow for execution by signature of at least two duly authorised officers, for deeds relating to the conveyancing of HDB flats.

sections.label: Mental Capacity Act remote witnessing
sections.summary: A new paragraph 1A lets the Public Guardian allow a donor to have electronic instrument execution witnessed remotely if stated criteria are met.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will do this by introducing a new paragraph 1A in the First Schedule to the Mental Capacity Act to provide that the Public Guardian may, on the application of a donor, allow him to have the execution of his electronic instrument witnessed remotely if all of the following criteria are satisfied.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, the donor must be under 75 years of age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, the proposed donee must belong to a legislated category of persons whose relationship with the donor makes it likely that the person will act in the donor's best interests, such as family members of the donor.

sections.label: Lawyer declares interest
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as a lawyer in property disputes and a partner at Rajah & Tann Singapore LLP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I declare my interest as a lawyer that acts in property-related disputes and a partner at Rajah & Tann Singapore LLP, a law firm that has a conveyancing practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces an important tool to simplify the conveyancing process.

sections.label: Electronic conveyancing option and payments
sections.summary: The Bill allows electronic issuance and exercise of options, payments into an electronic platform, and real time visibility of funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, having the option to perform various parts of the conveyancing transaction electronically should simplify the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill allows the seller to now issue an option electronically and for the buyer to exercise this option electronically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is also possible for payments to be made into an electronic platform, obviating the need for cheques and cashier’s orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Additionally, parties will have real time visibility over funds available from bank and in the CPF.

sections.label: Power of attorney family disputes
sections.summary: The Act treats a power of attorney given to a family member as suggesting low risk, though most reported disputes are among family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The only small caveat I would add is that the Act envisions that where the power of attorney is donated in favour of a family member, this is one of the factors that suggest that the transaction is low risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The only point I would make, which I am sure the Senior Minister of State is familiar with, is that based on the reported cases, most disputes around powers of attorney are disputes amongst family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope that presumption will not be given too much weight if there are many other family members who are not involved in the process.

sections.label: Clause 16 LPA Certificate Issuers
sections.summary: Clause 16 changes how LPAs can be issued by Certificate Issuers, who may be lawyers, psychiatrists or selected accredited doctors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 16 changes how LPAs can be issued by the Certificate Issuer which could either be lawyers, psychiatrists, or selected doctors accredited by the Public Guardian.

sections.label: Conditions and risk assessments for LPAs
sections.summary: Two conditions apply, on donor age and donee type, plus OPG assessments of no significant risk of fraud, incapacity or bad faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first two conditions are: one, that the donor must be under 75 years of age; and two, that the proposed donees must be either a professional donee working for remuneration, or be in specific family relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond that, the OPG also has to make an assessment that there is no significant risk in three aspects: one, that there is no significant risk of fraud or undue pressure on the donor to appoint particular donees; two, no significant risk that the donor lacks mental capacity; and three, no significant risk that the proposed donees will not act in the donor’s best interest.

sections.label: Remote signing and reporting risks
sections.summary: Remote signing increases risks, compounded because donees, unlike court-appointed deputies, need not report regularly to the OPG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My point, however, is that remote signing increases these risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This risk is also compounded by the fact that unlike deputies appointed by the court, donees appointed by donors need not make regular reports to the OPG on the status of the donor’s assets.

sections.label: LPA registration and vernacular outreach
sections.summary: Of 350,000 LPAs registered, Indian and Malay donors were 3% and 2%, prompting suggestions for vernacular outreach and MUIS involvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The data says that 350,000 LPAs have been registered as of 15 August this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, out of the 350,000, Indian and Malay donors only accounted for 3% and 2% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, other than the suggestions above, could the relevant Ministries also consider more vernacular outreach, perhaps through community organisations, to help more Singaporeans to understand the benefit of LPAs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And for the Malay/Muslim community specifically, could the Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) play a more active role in spreading awareness of the importance of making an LPA and also organising LPA information sessions.

sections.label: Errors, negligence claims and DCP take-up
sections.summary: Such errors can cause negligence claims and delays for buyers and sellers, and clarification is sought on the DCP take-up rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Such errors can lead to professional negligence claims, delays in buyers collecting their keys to commence the renovations and even for sellers receiving their proceeds later to purchase their next home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: That said, I seek clarification on the current take-up rate for DCP.

sections.label: DCP as sole conveyancing platform
sections.summary: Asks whether the DCP is intended to eventually be the only platform for conveyancing, as eLitigation is used today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My next clarification pertains to whether the DCP is intended to eventually be the only platform for conveyancing, the way how eLitigation is used today in the legal practice?

sections.label: Virtual execution of property deeds
sections.summary: New section 16W of the Bill would allow deeds relating to immovable property to be executed virtually on PETS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My next point is in respect of the new section 16W of the Bill which, if passed, will allow deeds relating to immovable property to be executed virtually on PETS.

sections.label: DCP safety safeguards for stakeholders
sections.summary: Asks how the Government will assure SMEs and elderly non-IT-savvy stakeholders of DCP safety and safeguards against abuse, scams and cybersecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Government: how will the Government assure stakeholders, especially those SMEs and elderly who are not IT savvy, of the safety and security of DCP, in particular, what are the safeguards against abuse, scams or cybersecurity threats? : Notwithstanding my clarifications, Mr Speaker, I stand in support of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill modernises how Singapore manages property transactions and legal authorisations.

sections.label: LPA audio-visual witnessing for under-75s
sections.summary: The Bill allows eligible individuals under 75 with appropriate donees to complete LPAs via live audio-visual witnessing under strict safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Law firms and banks have spoken about how one mortgage transaction can take up to 50 minutes just to check and reconcile documents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But the current LPA process still requires an in-person processing and witnessing which can be difficult for seniors with mobility issues or caregivers with limited time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill allows eligible individuals under 75 with appropriate donees, to complete their LPAs via live audio-visual witnessing, under strict safeguards.

sections.label: Digital navigators and Bill safeguards
sections.summary: Asks about community-based digital navigators or help channels, and notes the Bill introduces safeguards including secure electronic records and signatures definitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And will there be community-based digital navigators or help channels for those who need assistance?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill rightly mentions and introduces safeguards, such as the clear definitions for secure electronic records and signatures, requirements for attestation in digital witnessing and provisions for error correction and cybersecurity incidents under the amended SLA Act.

sections.label: DCP for electronic property transactions
sections.summary: The Bill facilitates implementation of a new DCP, allowing property transactions to be handled electronically.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It must make them more humane and more accessible for all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill facilitates the implementation of a new DCP, allowing property transactions to be handled electronically.

sections.label: Digital literacy study findings
sections.summary: A 2023 study found only 54% of respondents were confident using a new digital application on their own.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a 2023 study on Digital Literacy by the Centre for Research on Successful Ageing, only 54% of respondents were confident of using a new digital application on their own.

sections.label: PEXA fraud survey findings
sections.summary: A PEXA survey found 97% of respondents missed signs of fraudulent activity in their property transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a recent survey by PEXA, Australia's version of a digital conveyancing system, 97% of respondents missed signs of fraudulent activity in their property transactions.

sections.label: Remote witnessing LPA age condition
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes convenience for LPAs and notes remote witnessing requires the donor to be under 75.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the increased convenience for executing LPAs and hope this will encourage more Singaporeans to get their LPA done early to prepare for life's events or old age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that one condition for remote witnessing is that the donor must be under 75 years of age.

sections.label: DCP stakeholder ecosystem
sections.summary: DCP will bring together up to 17 different stakeholders into one united ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: DCP will bring together up to 17 different stakeholders, from lawyers, to banks, to HDB and SLA, into one united ecosystem.

sections.label: Assurance on new system charges
sections.summary: The question asks if the Minister can assure residents will not be burdened by new system charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, can the Minister assure the House that residents will not be burdened by new system charges and that measures, such as fee caps or subsidies, will be introduced, especially for first-time buyers or lower-income households?

sections.label: Remote witnessing location limit
sections.summary: Remote witnessing lets individuals execute documents electronically, but is limited to witnesses physically in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It allows individuals, especially seniors or persons with mobility challenges, to execute documents electronically without having to travel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, under section 16X of the Bill, remote witnessing is currently limited to witnesses physically located in Singapore.

sections.label: SLA correction of errors
sections.summary: Section 25 of the Bill empowers SLA to correct errors or omissions from system malfunctions or cybersecurity incidents after notifying affected parties and allowing representations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Section 25 of the Bill rightly empowers SLA to correct errors or omissions arising from system malfunctions or cybersecurity incidents after notifying affected parties and allowing representations.

sections.label: Opting out of public data
sections.summary: The passage asks whether individuals will have the option to opt out of having personal data publicly accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will individuals have the option to opt out of having personal data publicly accessible?

sections.label: Retention of conveyancing records
sections.summary: The passage asks whether digital conveyancing records will be archived indefinitely and remain accessible, and whether residents can download verified copies free of charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 23(5) of the amended SLA Act, records of conveyancing transactions must be retained for a prescribed period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister assure us that digital conveyancing records will be archived indefinitely and remain accessible to homeowners or their legal representatives, even after technology platforms evolve or vendors change?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can residents always download a verified, tamper-proof copy of their documents, free of charge, for their own safekeeping?

sections.label: OPG online LPA registrations
sections.summary: Since the OPG online system began in 2022, monthly LPA registrations have almost doubled, and in 2024 more than 95% of LPAs were made electronically.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of the OPG online system in 2022, we have observed that monthly LPA registrations have almost doubled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In 2024, more than 95% of LPAs were made electronically.

sections.label: Dementia prevalence and guardian alerts
sections.summary: MSF is guided by the 2024 WiSE study finding a significant increase in dementia prevalence among those aged 75 and above, matching more Public Guardian alerts for that group.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: MSF is guided by the 2024 study on the Well-Being of Singapore Elderly (WiSE) by the Institute of Mental Health, which found that there is a significant increase in the prevalence of dementia amongst those aged 75 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This also corresponds with our experience in practice, with the number of alerts to the Public Guardian on the well-being of individuals aged 75 and above, is about 3.5 times that those aged 65 to 74.

sections.label: Remote witnessing for LPAs
sections.summary: Remote witnessing will start with a smaller group of Certificate Issuers and donors before expanding, allowing training, preparation and user feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Based on earlier consultations, we anticipate that remote witnessing will be welcomed by members of the public who appreciate the greater convenience that it brings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To allow time for proper training and preparation, remote witnessing will start off with a smaller group of Certificate Issuers and donors before expanding to more Certificate Issuers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This gives us the chance to take in feedback from the users and further refine our processes and guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Over the years, the Government has implemented several enhancements to the process of making LPA, and we hope that with the expansion of remote witnessing, more will come forward to make an LPA, and this will provide greater assurance of care arrangements to their family members and their loved ones.

sections.label: SLA stakeholder engagement sessions
sections.summary: SLA has held more than 40 engagements with over 600 participants from relevant stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: To date, SLA has conducted more than 40 engagements with a cumulative attendance of more than 600 participants from relevant stakeholders.

sections.label: No DCP mandate plans
sections.summary: SLA is in discussion with relevant agencies but has no plans to mandate DCP use at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: While SLA is in discussion with the relevant agencies, there are no plans to mandate the use of the DCP at this juncture.

sections.label: DCP pilot fees and encouragement
sections.summary: SLA will consider efforts to encourage DCP use, and no additional fees or charges apply when the pilot is introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: SLA will also consider efforts to encourage the use of DCP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: There will also not be any additional fees or charges when the pilot is introduced.

sections.label: DCP personal and non-confidential data
sections.summary: No personal data will be publicly accessible on the DCP, and non-confidential data refers to publicly accessible information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Mr Yip asked whether individuals can opt out of having personal data publicly accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: There will be no personal data publicly accessible on the DCP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: To Mr Yip’s question on what constitutes “non-confidential” data that can be provided for transparency and analytics, this refers to information that is publicly accessible, such as property addresses, purchase prices, and information in the Land Register, which can be found through public searches today.

sections.label: DCP security features
sections.summary: The DCP is designed with enhanced security features to reduce the risks of scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The DCP is designed with enhanced security features to reduce the risks of scams.

sections.label: DCP charges review
sections.summary: Charges will have to be reviewed once the DCP is fully implemented as providing the service will cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: While this service is currently free, as I mentioned earlier in my speech, charges will have to be reviewed once the DCP is fully implemented as there will be a cost to providing this new service.

sections.label: Deed system not abolished
sections.summary: No common law country has abolished the deed, so abolishing the deed system will not be taken up at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As far as we are aware, no common law country has abolished the use of the deed altogether, so while I appreciate that there is a need to update some aspects of the system, particularly from wet ink to electronic signatures and the usage of red seals, to abolish the deed system altogether, it is something which we will not take up at this stage.

sections.label: Safeguards for electronic execution
sections.summary: Safeguards are being studied to protect the integrity of the electronic execution process of these documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Other than the benefits that will accrue to citizens, we are studying if and what safeguards are necessary to protect the integrity of the electronic execution process of each of these documents.

sections.label: Certificate Issuer written declaration
sections.summary: No video recording is required for the OPG, but the Certificate Issuer must declare the entire process in writing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: As of now, there is no requirement for provision or submission of a video recording to the OPG, but we do want to mandate that the Certificate Issuer make a declaration in writing of the entire process, as well as the points I have mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Legacy portal and Form One fee
sections.summary: The legacy portal's enhancement and the Form One registration fee waiver, free until 31 March 2026, are being considered for extension.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: So, on that point itself, whether the legacy portal can be able to be enhanced further, to serve this purpose in terms of the take-up rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: And finally, also, in relations to the take-up rate, the registration fee for Form One is currently free and waived until 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: In view that we are now rolling out this additional measure of remote certifications, whether we can consider to extend the waiver.

sections.label: Sitting suspended until 3.20 pm
sections.summary: The Sitting is suspended and the Chair will be taken at 3.20 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: My heart and my brain say the same thing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.20 pm.
